note: Description taken from Holmgren's 1910 original description of Eutermes aquilinus (in German), including the alate and two soldier size classes; the author uses head length measurements of 131 heads to demonstrate soldier dimorphism (a bimodal curve); type localities Blumenau and Jaraguá, Santa Catarina, Brazil. The original is in German and the BHL scan OCR is only moderate: decimal points are often misread as commas or colons and some measurement digits are blurred; blurred values are not cited. The species was then placed in Eutermes and is now in Nasutitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Large (alate with wings 21—22 mm, major soldier body length 4.5—5 mm, head length 2.15—2.60 mm); the soldier head capsule is nearly circular and glossy yellow, the nasus rather short, and head length shows a clearly bimodal distribution (minor soldiers 1.80—2.10 mm, major soldiers 2.15—2.60 mm), a classic example of soldier dimorphism in this genus; the alate compound eyes are large and prominent, the ocelli large and close to the compound eyes, and the cubitus has up to 20 branches.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut-brown, the postclypeus, labrum and antennae rusty yellow; thorax rusty yellow to rusty brown; abdominal tergites brown, sternites and legs rusty brown to straw-yellow. Wings with a yellowish brown tinge, white at the base between the media and cubitus. Cephalic bristles rather sparse, so the head is slightly glossy; bristles elsewhere rather dense; wing surface densely covered with very fine hairs and small spines. Head broadly oval; compound eyes large, prominent; ocelli large, very close to the compound eyes; frontal marks long, slit-like; the muscle scars at the transverse band form a small arc in front of the frontal marks. Postclypeus relatively long, but less than half its width. Antennae 15-segmented: segment 3 almost as long as segment 2, segment 4 as long as segment 2 but thicker and subspherical. Pronotum wider than the head (without eyes) and slightly narrower than the head (with eyes), slightly longer than half its width, anterior margin almost completely straight, posterior margin rather broad and straight, only indistinctly concave. Wings long; below the radial sector there is a diffuse yellow line; media close to the cubitus, with one to several branches at its end, one of them reaching the end of the radius sector; cubitus with up to 20 branches, the inner 8 thickened and long, very oblique and very dense. Measurements: body length (with wings) 21—22 mm; head length 1.95 mm; from the anterior margin of the transverse band to the occiput 1.2 mm (the head width figure is damaged in the OCR and is not cited).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head capsule glossy yellow, nasus brown, antennae yellowish; body white to white-yellow. Head with rather dense short hairs, a few longer bristles at the base of the nasus and on the vertex; body also with rather dense short hairs, the posterior margins of the abdominal tergites with longer bristles. Head large, nearly circular; frontal outline a weakly convex line, the elevation at the base of the nasus almost imperceptible. Antennae 13-segmented: the basal segment equal to the sum of the next two, segment 3 slightly longer than segment 2, segment 4 shorter than segment 2, segment 5 as long as segment 3 but thicker at its upper end. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior margin not concave. Measurements: body length 4.5—5 mm; head length 2.15—2.60 mm (modal class 2.40—2.45 mm). Minor soldier: same colour and pilosity as the major soldier, only smaller; measurements: body length 4 mm; head length 1.80—2.10 mm (modal class 1.95—2.00 mm). The head width figures for both classes are damaged in the OCR and are not cited.
